content: Hi! How can I help you today with your SQL queries?
Hi. I want to make a report that lists customers and their order dates. Can you help me write that query?
Absolutely. Could you share the table names and which columns you'd like included in your report?
Sure. We have a 'customers' table and an 'orders' table. I'd like to show the customer's name and each of their order dates.

Thanks! Assuming 'customers' has a 'name' column and 'orders' has 'order_date' and a foreign key 'customer_id', here's a read-only, parameterized query:
```sql
SELECT c.name, o.order_date
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id;
```
Nice. What if I just want customers who have placed at least one order?

The query I shared already only lists customers with orders, because it uses an INNER JOIN. Alternatively, you can use EXISTS for the same effect:
```sql
SELECT name
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id);
```
Got it. How would I show customers who haven't ordered anything yet?

You can use a LEFT JOIN and filter for NULLs in the 'orders' table:
```sql
SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;
```
Could I include their email too? We have a column called 'email'.

Definitely. Just add 'c.email' to the SELECT clause. For example:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;
```
Is it okay to show full emails, or should I mask them for compliance reasons?

Great question! For PII compliance, it's safer to mask part of the email. Here's an example using SQL substring functions:
```sql
SELECT c.name, CONCAT(LEFT(c.email, 2), '***', SUBSTRING(c.email, CHARINDEX('@', c.email), LEN(c.email))) AS masked_email
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;
```
I like that. Can I also see how many orders each customer made, even if it's zero?

Sure! You can aggregate with COUNT and GROUP BY, like this:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email;
```
If I want to filter for customers with more than 2 orders, should I use WHERE or HAVING?

Use HAVING because you're filtering on the aggregated count:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 2;
```
Is there a way to write this as a parameterized query, so I can set the minimum order count at runtime?

Yes! Use a parameter for the minimum count. For example, in a parameterized environment:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > @min_order_count;
```
